data.title: Anthropic IPO to move forward despite tech selloff: FT
data.description:
Anthropic is pressing ahead with its plans for a U.S. public listing this month and is even prepared to accept a lower-than-expected valuation amid investor worries over an ongoing tech selloff, The Financial Times reported, citing multiple investors in the AI startup.

The Claude maker is racing towards its much-anticipated initial public offering before the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday this month, the investors said, adding that the company is planning to raise $80B-$100B at a valuation of $1.25T-$1.75T.

While that is a significant increase from its current $965B valuation, the target falls short of the doubled price tag investors had hoped for as recently as a month ago.

“My view is they will price it very conservatively, call it $1.5tn, and go up from there,” said one large investor. Others taking part in the deal expected even a lower valuation of roughly $1.3T.

Anthropic’s scaled-back expectations coincide with a sharp decline in AI-related tech stocks over the recent weeks, a selloff that accelerated on Thursday when the Nasdaq 100 plunged 6.4% on worries over a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure buildout.

Bloomberg reported on Friday that OpenAI , which recently delayed its IPO plans, completed a new private funding round of roughly $11B, valuing the ChatGPT maker at $1.25T, a sharp decline from $30B or more it initially sought at a $1.4T valuation.

However, according to more than half a dozen Anthropic investors, the company remains on track to go public even if its CEO Dario Amodei has to accept a price cut to achieve the goal.

“It’s just one milestone along the way,” one early investor of the company said. “They should treat it like every other fundraise: a means to an end.”

Multiple people familiar with Amodei’s thinking said that the CEO has shown little interest in beating Elon Musk’s SpaceX , which completed the largest ever IPO in June at a valuation of roughly $1.8T. “They don’t care about being bigger than SpaceX or maximizing the IPO,” one investor noted.

“They’re donating the majority of their economics to charity anyway,” he added, referring to Anthropic co-founders’ intention to hand 80% of their personal equity in the company to charitable purposes.

With $150B in cash and liquid investments on its balance sheet, Anthropic expects to raise enough funding so as not to sell equity again, people familiar with its thinking said.

“Public markets are highly averse to dilution,” added another large investor. “When you are taking a company public, that should be the last time you tap equity capital markets. But it opens the window for debt.”

JPMorgan , which leads U.S. retail sales of company shares, is expected to hold an “information session” for prospective investors on November 13, the FT said. Anthropic declined to comment on the report.

data.title: Ether ETFs Face Another $99.9M Outflow as Demand Stays Uneven
data.description:
TL;DR: US spot Ether ETFs posted a $99.9 million net outflow on November 5, Farside data show, following an $85.3 million outflow on November 3 and a temporary recovery on November 4. The pattern highlights a fragile demand picture, but cannot establish a direct forecast for ETH’s price.

Ether’s exchange-traded fund market is still searching for consistency. The latest fully reported daily figures in Farside Investors’ Ether ETF table show a $99.9 million net withdrawal on Thursday, November 5, just a day after the same group recorded a $53 million inflow. The reversal demonstrates why single-session data need context.

November 6’s table still contained unreported fields when reviewed, so it would be misleading to present the partial figure as a final market-wide total. A dated, complete session offers a better basis for an editorial assessment.

A brief rebound gave way to renewed redemptions

On November 5, BlackRock’s ETHA recorded a $75.2 million outflow and the firm’s ETHB line showed a further $22 million leaving. Fidelity’s FETH was down $2.2 million, while Grayscale’s ETHE showed a modest $500,000 withdrawal. Those figures add up to the $99.9 million negative session.

The previous day looked different. On November 4, the listed products collectively brought in $53 million, with positive flows in several funds offsetting negative readings elsewhere. Before that, November 2 and 3 brought losses of $139.7 million and $85.3 million respectively. The emerging picture is not a perfectly uninterrupted exodus. It is a market in which intermittent buying has yet to overcome repeated bouts of selling.

Our earlier report on November 2’s Ether ETF withdrawals provides a useful baseline. The subsequent sessions show that the pressure has persisted but has also varied substantially between days and issuers.

What ETF activity does and does not reveal

An ETF’s reported flow measures changes in the investment wrapper, not all Ethereum transactions. Institutions can obtain ETH exposure through spot holdings, derivatives, treasury companies and other vehicles. A negative day in the US listed fund category does not prove every sophisticated investor has turned bearish.

This is especially important for Ethereum because a significant share of the network’s economic activity occurs independently of an ETF. Stablecoin transfers, decentralised exchanges, tokenised assets and staking continue to operate whatever happens to a particular fund’s share count. The long-term investment case for ETH is often tied to that activity, but there is no automatic formula linking application usage to the token’s short-term price.

Concentration adds another layer. If one manager dominates the day’s net withdrawals, the aggregate should not be described as a consensus of all issuers. Analysts also need to separate price moves from flows: the dollar value of assets in a fund can fall because of market prices even when investors have not redeemed an equivalent amount of shares.

Two separate stories to follow

The first is whether ETF investors return in size and for more than a single session. The second is what happens in Ethereum’s development roadmap. The Ethereum Foundation announced a Glamsterdam testing delay on November 6, citing concerns about how proposed gas changes could affect existing applications. That is an engineering issue, not proof of a market-flow response, and it should be covered on its own terms.

For traders and longer-term holders, the practical takeaway is to compare several fully reported sessions, assess which issuers are driving the moves and resist treating flows as a stand-alone trading signal. Thursday’s number is meaningful evidence of weaker demand through US funds; it is not a reliable prediction of ETH’s next move.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: CIRL Appoints Ashish Sardesai As MD And CEO
data.description:
The insurance industry veteran brings over 25 years of experience as the CDSL subsidiary looks to expand its repository business and deepen partnerships with insurers

Centrico Insurance Repository Limited (CIRL), a subsidiary of Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL), has appointed Ashish Sardesai as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, effective 2 November 2026. The appointment comes as the company looks to strengthen its position in the insurance repository segment, expand its industry partnerships and enhance the digital services available to policyholders.

Sardesai brings more than 25 years of professional experience across life insurance, financial services, business development and technology-led enterprises. Over the course of his career, he has held senior leadership positions at several organisations in the insurance and financial services sectors, including Edelweiss Tokio Life Insurance, Tata AIA Life Insurance, Max New York Life Insurance and AIBCL (India) Insurance Broking. His experience spans business strategy, institutional partnerships, market development and building business operations across different segments of the financial services industry.

In addition to his experience in the insurance sector, Sardesai has founded and led an AI-powered skill-tech platform, giving him exposure to technology-led business models and digital enterprise development. His professional background combines insurance industry knowledge with experience in business development and technology-driven initiatives.

His appointment comes at a time when CIRL's insurance repository operations are expanding. As of 30 September 2026, the company had approximately 26.10 lakh electronic insurance accounts and partnerships with 49 insurance companies. The growing account base and insurer network reflect the increasing adoption of electronic insurance records and the industry's gradual shift towards digital policy management.

Insurance repositories enable policyholders to maintain their insurance policies in electronic form, reducing dependence on physical documents and making policy information easier to access and manage. Through its repository services, CIRL works with insurers to facilitate the electronic holding of insurance policies and improve the overall policyholder experience.

Sardesai's appointment is expected to strengthen the company's leadership as it focuses on expanding its repository business, building relationships across the insurance ecosystem and improving the delivery of digital insurance services.

data.title: Tata Steel Q2 Profit Rises 16%; Noel Tata To Retire As Vice-Chairman
data.description:
Tata Steel's consolidated revenue rises 11.5 per cent to Rs 65,436 crore in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA grows 17 per cent year-on-year to Rs 10,665 crore; Noel Tata to step down on November 11

Tata Steel posted a 16.2 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter of FY27, supported by higher revenue and improved operating performance, while Noel Naval Tata is set to retire as the company's vice-chairman on November 11.

Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rose to Rs 3,699.59 crore in the July-September quarter, compared with Rs 3,183.09 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal, the company said in a regulatory filing on Friday.

Revenue from operations increased 11.5 per cent to Rs 65,436.24 crore from Rs 58,689.29 crore a year earlier.

Consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) stood at Rs 10,665 crore, with a margin of around 16 per cent. EBITDA increased 17 per cent year-on-year and 14 per cent sequentially.

In India, revenue stood at Rs 42,653 crore, while EBITDA was Rs 10,634 crore, translating into an operating margin of 25 per cent.

Crude steel production in India increased 7 per cent sequentially to 6.18 million tonnes during the quarter, while deliveries rose 16 per cent to 5.98 million tonnes, reflecting improved production and sales volumes.

The company incurred capital expenditure of around Rs 3,280 crore during the quarter, taking its first-half spending to Rs 6,860 crore.

Key projects under execution include the 4.8 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) capacity expansion at Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited, a 0.7 MTPA Hot Rolled Pickling and Galvanising Line, and a 300,000-tonne tinplate expansion.

Tata Steel's net debt stood at Rs 91,423 crore at the end of the quarter, with its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio at 2.4 times. Group liquidity was Rs 40,076 crore, including cash and cash equivalents of around Rs 10,300 crore.

Separately, Noel Naval Tata will retire as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director and Vice-Chairman of the board with effect from the close of business hours on November 11, 2026.

T V Narendran, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Tata Steel, said the company continued to advance its volume and value growth strategy in India, supported by customer engagement and a resilient supply chain despite geopolitical and economic uncertainties and elevated raw material costs.

He said the automotive and special products businesses delivered a strong performance, while downstream sales continued to grow. The company is also expanding its presence in emerging segments, including shipbuilding, data centres and containers.

Narendran added that the company was making steady progress on its capacity expansion and downstream growth projects.

data.title: Temasek Sells 3.74% Stake In CarTrade Tech For Rs 470 Cr
data.description:
MacRitchie Investments' holding in the auto platform declined to 3.08 per cent from 6.82 per cent, while Capital Group and Norway's sovereign wealth fund bought shares worth Rs 445 crore

Singapore's state-owned investment firm Temasek has divested a 3.74 per cent stake in multi-channel automobile platform CarTrade Tech for Rs 470.10 crore through an open market transaction.

Temasek, through its affiliate MacRitchie Investments Pte Ltd, sold 18.20 lakh shares of Navi Mumbai-based CarTrade Tech at an average price of Rs 2,583 apiece, according to bulk deal data available on the BSE on Friday.

Following the transaction, MacRitchie Investments' holding in CarTrade Tech declined to 3.08 per cent from 6.82 per cent.

Capital Group, Norway Fund Buy Shares

On the buying side, US-based Capital Group, through its arm SmallCap World Fund Inc, and Norway's Government Pension Fund Global jointly acquired more than 17.23 lakh shares, representing a 3.54 per cent stake in CarTrade Tech.

The shares were purchased at an average price of Rs 2,583 apiece, taking the combined transaction value to approximately Rs 445 crore.

Shares of CarTrade Tech rose 3.72 per cent to close at Rs 2,699.30 apiece on the BSE on Friday.

data.title: Prestige Estates Acquires Allure Developers For Rs 524 Cr
data.description:
The acquisition gives Prestige Estates full ownership of a company developing a residential project in Noida Sector 150, with payment to be made in tranches

Real estate developer Prestige Estates Projects has acquired a 100 per cent stake in Allure Developers for up to Rs 523.76 crore, adding a residential project in Noida's Sector 150 to its portfolio as part of its expansion in Delhi-NCR.

In a regulatory filing, Prestige Estates said it entered into a share purchase agreement on 6 November 2026 to acquire the entire equity share capital of Allure Developers. Following the transaction, Allure has become a wholly owned subsidiary of Prestige Estates.

The consideration of up to Rs 523.76 crore will be paid in tranches. Allure is undertaking the development of a residential project in Noida Sector 150.

Recent Acquisition Activity

The acquisition follows Prestige Estates' purchase of 100 per cent equity in Gloind Vintage Infra for an enterprise value of Rs 519 crore through its subsidiary, Prestige Retail Ventures.

Following the completion of that transaction, Prestige Estates will indirectly hold Gloind's equity share capital. It will also have indirect ownership and control of 100 per cent of Tarun Realtors, a subsidiary of Gloind Vintage Infra.

Tarun Realtors owns a shopping mall in Bengaluru.

Prestige Estates reported a 44 per cent decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 256.2 crore for the quarter ended September, compared with Rs 457.4 crore in the corresponding period of the previous year.

The company's total income declined to Rs 2,222.2 crore in the second quarter of the current financial year from Rs 2,697.8 crore a year earlier, according to its regulatory filing.

For the April-September period, consolidated net profit fell to Rs 527.6 crore from Rs 768.9 crore in the corresponding period of the previous year.

Total income for the first half of the financial year declined to Rs 5,057.8 crore from Rs 5,166.5 crore in the year-ago period.

data.title: SoftBank Plans ChatGPT Rollout For Employees Amid AI Push
data.description:
SB Energy will deploy OpenAI tools across its workforce as the SoftBank-backed company expands its role in the Stargate AI infrastructure project

SoftBank-backed SB Energy plans to deploy OpenAI's artificial intelligence tools, including ChatGPT, for its employees as part of a broader partnership linked to the ambitious Stargate AI infrastructure project. The development highlights the growing adoption of generative AI within corporate workforces as companies increasingly integrate the technology into everyday business operations.

Under the partnership, SB Energy will use OpenAI's application programming interfaces (APIs) and make ChatGPT available to employees. The company is also expected to build and operate a 1.2-gigawatt data centre facility in Milam County, Texas, as part of the collaboration.

The employee deployment reflects how AI infrastructure investments are increasingly translating into workplace technology adoption, with businesses exploring ways to integrate AI into internal workflows, improve productivity and support operational efficiency.

The partnership comes amid heightened tensions between Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. Musk has publicly accused SoftBank of defaulting on payments for turbine orders linked to the Stargate project, although he has not provided details substantiating the allegation. SoftBank is among the major investors backing OpenAI and the proposed $500 billion AI infrastructure initiative.

The developments underline the growing intersection of AI infrastructure expansion and enterprise workforce transformation, as companies look to embed generative AI tools into employee workflows.

data.title: Prestige Estates Takes Over Allure Developers In Rs 524 Cr Acquisition Deal
data.description:
The acquisition gives Prestige Estates complete ownership of Allure Developers and its ongoing residential project in Noida

Prestige Estates Projects has acquired a 100 per cent stake in Allure Developers Pvt Ltd for Rs 523.76 crore, strengthening its residential portfolio in the Delhi-NCR market. The acquisition gives the Bengaluru-based real estate developer control of a residential project being developed in Noida's Sector 150.

The company entered into a share purchase agreement on November 6, 2026, to acquire the entire equity share capital of Allure Developers, according to a regulatory filing. Following the transaction, Allure Developers has become a wholly owned subsidiary of Prestige Estates, with the consideration to be paid in tranches.

The acquisition is part of Prestige Estates' expansion strategy and adds to its recent investments across different real estate segments. The company has been pursuing acquisitions to expand its development portfolio and strengthen its presence in key property markets.

The latest transaction follows Prestige Estates' acquisition of 100 per cent equity in Gloind Vintage Infra for an enterprise value of Rs 519 crore. The deal was executed through its subsidiary, Prestige Retail Ventures, as part of the group's investment activity.

Upon completion, Prestige Estates will indirectly hold the entire equity share capital of Gloind Vintage Infra. The transaction will also give it indirect ownership and control of Tarun Realtors, a subsidiary of Gloind that owns a shopping mall in Bengaluru.

Quarterly Profit Declines

The acquisitions come against the backdrop of a decline in the company's financial performance during the September quarter. Prestige Estates reported a 44 per cent year-on-year fall in consolidated net profit to Rs 256.2 crore for the quarter, compared with Rs 457.4 crore in the corresponding period last year.

The company's total income also declined during the quarter, falling to Rs 2,222.2 crore from Rs 2,697.8 crore in the year-ago period, according to the regulatory filing. The decline in both profit and income reflects the company's performance during the second quarter of the current financial year.

For the April-September period, consolidated net profit fell to Rs 527.6 crore from Rs 768.9 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. Total income during the first half also declined to Rs 5,057.8 crore from Rs 5,166.5 crore a year earlier.

data.title: JSW Dulux Reports 21.3% Revenue Growth In Q2 FY27 On Strong Paint Market Demand
data.description:
The company recorded 21 per cent volume growth, with festive demand supporting decorative paints and infrastructure, energy and automotive sectors driving industrial coatings

JSW Dulux reported revenue from operations of Rs 961.9 crore in the second quarter of FY27, registering a 21.3 per cent increase over Rs 793.3 crore in the corresponding period last year on a comparable retained-business basis. Volume grew 21 per cent, supported by demand across its decorative and industrial paints businesses.

The company’s performance comes amid increased festive-season traction in the decorative paints segment. According to the company, all decorative paint categories witnessed strong demand ahead of the festive season. It also continued to report market share gains across its businesses.

Industrial paints performance was supported by demand from the infrastructure and energy sectors. In automotive coatings, the company reported customer wins and expansion into new verticals, strengthening its presence in the segment.

Despite revenue growth, profitability remained under pressure from elevated raw material costs. Comparable EBITDA from operations rose 4.4 per cent to Rs 110.9 crore from Rs 106.3 crore in the year-ago quarter. Profit after tax (PAT), excluding exceptional items, increased 2 per cent to Rs 71.2 crore.

Rajiv Rajgopal, Joint Managing Director and CEO, JSW Dulux, says, “We delivered consecutive quarter of double-digit volume and value growth, reflecting steady progress on our strategic priorities. We continued to make steady market share gains across our businesses. In Decorative Paints, all categories witnessed strong traction leading up to the festive season. Industrial Paints performance was aided by strong demand in infrastructure and energy sectors. We saw gains in automotive space with customer wins and entry into new verticals.”

He adds that the company has undertaken calibrated price increases to partly offset the impact of raw material inflation. “Despite these headwinds, comparable EBITDA grew 4.4 percent through prudent balance between cost management and growth initiatives. However, as geopolitical disturbances continue to affect raw material inflation, we will keep evaluating the situation and implementing calibrated price increases.”

For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations increased 20 per cent to Rs 1,926.9 crore on a comparable retained-business basis, while volume growth stood at 23 per cent. EBITDA from operations rose 9.4 per cent to Rs 226 crore, and PAT excluding exceptional items increased 50.5 per cent to Rs 206.7 crore. The first-half PAT includes dividend income of Rs 55.9 crore from the company’s subsidiary, ICI India Research and Technology Centre.

On the product front, the company launched VT Soft Sheen across India under its Accessible Luxury portfolio, combining its TruColour proposition with an eight-year Dulux Assurance warranty. Its Automotive and Specialty Coatings business also introduced the EONIX Rubbing and Polishing Compound range, expanding into adjacent categories within original equipment manufacturer-authorised workshop networks.

The company said elevated raw material inflation and geopolitical developments remain key factors influencing its pricing decisions and margins as it moves through the remainder of the financial year.

data.title: Arjun Verma Takes Charge As GP Petroleums Managing Director
data.description:
Verma, who previously served as Executive Director, will lead the company’s core businesses and evaluate expansion opportunities in India and overseas

GP Petroleums Limited (GPPL) has appointed Arjun Verma as its Managing Director, effective 27 October 2026. Verma was previously serving as the company’s Executive Director.

In his new role, Verma will lead the company’s business verticals, with a focus on strengthening its existing operations and evaluating expansion opportunities in domestic and overseas markets. The company said its plans could include strategic investments and acquisitions, with an emphasis on capital allocation, profitable growth and improving cash flows.

A Chartered Accountant with more than 35 years of experience, Verma has been involved in shaping GPPL’s financial strategy and supporting its governance and business initiatives.

Ayush Goel, Executive Chairman and Whole-Time Director of GP Petroleums, said Verma’s understanding of the company and financial expertise would support its focus on strengthening core businesses and improving shareholder returns.

Q2 Performance

The leadership change comes after GPPL reported a rise in its financial performance for the second quarter of FY27.

The company’s profit after tax (PAT) increased 179 per cent year-on-year to Rs 15.3 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 5.5 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

Revenue rose 124 per cent to Rs 340.8 crore from Rs 152.4 crore in Q2 FY26.

data.title: French presidential hopeful Melenchon pledges minimum wage rise, retirement at 60
data.description:
Key points:
  • Vows to lift net monthly minimum wage to €1,700
  • Would eventually restore retirement at 60
  • Calls for withdrawal of France from NATO

By Mathieu Rosemain

Jean-Luc Melenchon, the hard-left French presidential hopeful, will pledge to raise the minimum wage and restore the country's retirement age to 60 when he launches his 2027 election programme on Saturday.

Melenchon, 75, is viewed as the strongest contender on the left and recent opinion polls have shown him reaching the presidential runoff next April against Marine Le Pen on the far-right, but also indicate he would lose in the second round.

His manifesto, titled "L'Avenir en commun" ("A Shared Future"), is the fifth edition of the platform of his party, France Unbowed (LFI), and largely reaffirms policies that have formed the backbone of Melenchon's previous presidential bids.

Among its flagship pledges is the repeal of President Emmanuel Macron's pension reform, which gradually raised France's minimum retirement age from 62 to 64 in an effort to shore up public finances.

LFI says it would restore retirement at 60 for people who have contributed to the system for 40 years.

The programme also calls for increasing the net monthly minimum wage to €1,700 from around €1,480 and includes plans to abolish the flat tax on capital income, raise taxes on the wealthiest households and cap prices for essential foods.

LFI also reiterates its support for a gradual phase-out of nuclear power in favour of a fully renewable electricity system, including scrapping the planned EPR2 reactor programme and not extending the lifespan of nuclear plants beyond 60 years.

On foreign policy, Melenchon's programme reiterates his long-standing criticism of NATO and calls for France's gradual withdrawal from the alliance, starting with an exit from its integrated military command.

It also criticises German influence on European Union economic policy, describing Berlin as Europe's chief defender of "ordoliberalism", an economic philosophy centred on strict budget rules, price stability and independent monetary policy.

The programme calls for greater protection of domestic industry, including measures to encourage the relocation of production to France, and advocates a more interventionist role for the state in the economy.

data.title: Heavy rain floods tents housing Gaza displaced people, aid shortages hamper response
data.description:
Key points:
  • Many displaced Palestinians' tents flooded after rain
  • Hamas blames Israel for lack of shelters and materials
  • Israeli agency says it has sought to improve conditions

By Dawoud Abu Alkas and Nidal al-Mughrabi

Heavy rains have flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians crammed into encampments across the Gaza Strip, washing away shelters and soaking blankets and mattresses, local authorities said on Saturday.

The Hamas-run Gaza government media office said at least 70,000 tents had been flooded in the past 12 hours, affecting tens of thousands of displaced people and causing injuries although no fatalities had been reported.

The territory's civil defence service said it had received 1,500 distress calls from displaced residents. Three abandoned houses collapsed without causing injuries, it added.

At a tent encampment in Gaza City, some people tried to repair their tents, while others used sand to reinforce them and prevent water from entering. Some were busy getting their children out of flooded tents.

Olfat Magdoub, a Gaza resident, tried in vain to sweep water away from her tent.

"This is the first day of rain, and of course we are already flooded. What will happen if it rains again the next day? This is only the first day and we're already overwhelmed," said the woman.

"Two weeks ago when it rained, I swear to God, I spent four days sleeping on blankets spread on the floor because the rainwater had flooded the bedding. Same now, the mattresses are wet so we sleep on the ground.”

Municipal and civil defence officials said they were unable to cope with the storm because of fuel shortages and damage to equipment.

They said Israel had destroyed hundreds of vehicles, including bulldozers and others used to pump water, during its war against Hamas, which had displaced most of the territory's more than 2 million residents and left much of Gaza in ruins. Most of the population now lives in tent camps.

Hamas blamed Israel for not allowing shelters and construction materials into Gaza.

COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, did not immediately comment on the accusations by Hamas. It said in a statement on Friday that it had stepped up efforts to improve sanitary conditions across Gaza before the heavy rain, which had been expected, in coordination with international organisations.

LITTLE PROGRESS ON RECONSTRUCTION

The agency said four additional vacuum trucks entered Gaza this week through the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), joining eight others brought in over the past month to support sewage pumping, weekly waste removal and repairs to water and sewage infrastructure.

A US-brokered ceasefire last year called for the eventual reconstruction of Gaza, but little progress has been made. Negotiators have failed to agree on terms for Hamas to disarm or for Israel to withdraw its troops, which control about two-thirds of the territory and from which residents have been ordered to leave.

"We have no resources, no tarpaulins, no tents and no one is checking on us," said displaced Gaza resident Rafiq Ghattas, standing barefoot in the middle of a large pool of rainwater.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel began its assault on the territory after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on attacks on October 7, 2023.

data.title: Elon Musk's bankruptcy warnings collide with JPMorgan's first Bitcoin forecast
data.description:
Elon Musk has a new item on his worry list. The Tesla and SpaceX chief, described by Forbes as the world's first trillionaire, has paired his long-running warnings about financial collapse with fresh fears about an artificial intelligence-driven nightmare.

His latest message is a warning of "global bankruptcy." Forbes suggests it could become a game-changer for the Bitcoin price, and it lands just as JPMorgan rolls out a Bitcoin forecast that Forbes called "extraordinary."

During a February 2026 appearance on the Dwarkesh Podcast, he put his confidence level well past the usual scale.

"We are 1000% going to go bankrupt as a country and fail as a country without AI and robots."

Musk's view is that the US cannot outgrow its debt with today's economy. Only a big jump in productivity from AI and robotics would let the country cover what it owes. Without that jump, he argues, the bill eventually wins.

US national debt passed $40 trillion in late 2026, according to the research findings. Interest payments on that debt are reported to exceed military spending.

This is where Musk's two fears meet. He frames AI as both a possible threat and the only realistic escape hatch from the debt spiral.

JPMorgan Asset Management included Bitcoin in its Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report for the first time in October 2026. That annual report is where the firm lays out its expected returns for major asset classes over the coming decade.

The headline figure: a projected 10% annualized return for Bitcoin through 2036. The research findings note that this outpaces JPMorgan's forecasts for traditional holdings such as large-cap US stocks and bonds.

The reasoning rests on supply. Bitcoin's issuance is capped, while the broader money supply keeps expanding.

That logic lines up neatly with how Musk talks about Bitcoin. He has described it as "based on energy" and contrasted it with fiat currency, which governments can print without a hard limit.

Tesla holds 11,509 BTC, while SpaceX holds 18,712 BTC, according to the research findings. Together that comes to approximately 30,221 BTC, reportedly acquired at low average costs.

That gives Musk a direct stake in how markets interpret his warnings. Few public figures warning about fiscal collapse also run two companies sitting on a large position in the asset most often pitched as a hedge against it.

To be fair, there is no evidence that his statements are designed to move the market. But anyone reading his posts should know where the corporate treasuries sit.

The connection between government debt and Bitcoin is not new. Bitcoin's original design was a response to concerns about centralized money and unchecked issuance.

The research findings are explicit that no single Musk statement has been conclusively tied to an immediate Bitcoin price move.

The most significant development here is arguably JPMorgan's, not Musk's. A formal return assumption from JPMorgan Asset Management is different. Long-term capital market assumptions feed into how advisers and institutions think about portfolio construction. Bitcoin showing up in that framework signals that it is being treated as an asset class worth modeling, rather than a curiosity.

A 10% forecast is also not a guarantee. Forecasts of this kind are long-range estimates, and a decade is plenty of time for assumptions to break.

For now, the practical watch list is short. Track US fiscal policy and debt-servicing costs, monitor whether other large asset managers follow JPMorgan in publishing Bitcoin assumptions, and keep an eye on any changes to Tesla's and SpaceX's holdings.

data.title: FDA Investigates Cancer Risk Associated With Novartis' Zolgensma Gene Therapy
data.description:
BASEL (dpa-AFX) - In medicine, one truth transcends time: a drug's worth is measured not merely by how effectively it fights disease, but also by how safely it does so.

One medicine that has recently drawn the FDA's attention over emerging safety concerns is Novartis Inc.'s (NVS) Zolgensma gene therapy.

Approved in the U.S. in May 2019, Zolgensma is an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of pediatric patients less than 2 years of age with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). Administered as a one-time intravenous infusion, Zolgensma carries a boxed warning for serious liver injury and acute liver failure, including reported fatal cases. Its prescribing information also highlights several other important safety concerns, including elevated aminotransferases, thrombocytopenia, thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), and the potential risk of tumorigenicity associated with AAV vector integration.

More than 6,000 patients have been treated with Zolgensma across clinical trials, managed access programs and commercial treatment, according to Novartis. Priced at $2.125 million for a one-time treatment, Zolgensma made headlines in 2019 as the world's most expensive drug at the time.

On November 5, 2026, Novartis disclosed that it had received nine reports of tumors in patients previously treated with Zolgensma since the therapy's first approval in 2019. Of these, two cases have so far shown evidence of vector DNA integration into the patients' DNA. Both patients have undergone treatment and remain under medical monitoring.

Postmarketing reports of tumor formation (neoplasia) include tumors of the central and peripheral nervous systems, spinal/paraspinal regions, and the kidney. Further investigation revealed that, in two cases, product-related vector DNA integration involved the GLI1 (Glioma-Associated Oncogene Homolog 1) gene, an oncogene that has the potential to cause cancer when overexpressed or abnormally activated. The mechanism underlying GLI1 overexpression in the third case remains under investigation.

Novartis has another approved gene therapy, Itvisma, which uses the same vector and construct as Zolgensma.

Itvisma is indicated for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in adult and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older with a confirmed mutation in the survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) gene. Administered via intrathecal injection, Itvisma is also an AAV vector-based gene therapy. It was approved by the FDA in November 2025 and is priced at $2.59 million per treatment.

Itvisma carries a boxed warning for acute serious liver injury and elevated aminotransferases. Its prescribing information also includes warnings and precautions regarding hepatotoxicity (liver injury), thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), peripheral sensory neuropathy, thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), elevated cardiac troponin I, and AAV vector integration and the potential risk of tumorigenicity.

During the first nine months of 2026, Novartis reported combined sales of $1.071 billion for its Zolgensma Group, comprising Zolgensma and Itvisma, compared with $925 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

With postmarketing adverse event reports of malignancies in patients treated with Zolgensma, the FDA has begun an investigation of the identified risk of neoplasia, including malignancy, with serious outcomes.

The FDA has determined that the risk of neoplasia, including malignancy, applies to both Zolgensma and Itvisma, as they contain the same vector and construct. To date, no cases of neoplasia have been reported following Itvisma administration.

The overall benefits of both Zolgensma and Itvisma continue to outweigh their potential risks for their respective approved indications. Nevertheless, the agency is evaluating whether further regulatory action is warranted.

As part of this assessment, the FDA is expeditiously reviewing whether Zolgensma's current prescribing information and long-term follow-up studies are adequate to address the newly identified risk of insertional oncogenesis. The agency has also advised that patients treated with the therapy and clinical trial participants be monitored for tumor formation.

According to a review published in the Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics in July of 2026, a total of 78 marketed drugs were withdrawn by the FDA between 1955 and 2026, frequently associated with serious adverse effects.

As the FDA investigation unfolds, the implications for Zolgensma, Itvisma, and the broader landscape of AAV-based gene therapies remain an important area to watch.

data.title: China extends gold buying spree to two years as prices drop, adds 25.8 tonnes in October
data.description:
China’s central bank added to its gold reserves in October — extending a buying streak to two years — as the precious metal fell almost 7% to end the month below the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold.

Bullion holdings at the People’s Bank of China rose by 830,000 ounces in October, or around 25.8 metric tons, according to official data released Saturday. That’s the 24th consecutive month of accumulation. In particular, the central bank has stepped up purchases in recent months as gold prices have slumped, with additions in the first 10 months of the year totaling around 129 metric tons.

PBOC was the biggest disclosed buyer among global central banks in the third quarter, World Gold Council data showed. Cumulative official-sector purchases reported by the WGC were a net 321 tons in the July to September period, the most since the final quarter of 2024. These accumulations remain a key support to gold prices in an otherwise tepid market.

Bullion touched a one-year low last month and recorded its biggest October decline since the global financial crisis in 2008. It’s rebounded since the US midterm elections this week, but remains down by more than a fifth since the Iran war began in late February. Higher energy prices have fueled inflation and led to tighter monetary policy, which is typically a headwind for non-yielding bullion.

PBOC’s holdings influence the buying patterns of Chinese households. Many purchased gold at around $4,000 an ounce in October, expecting that central-bank purchasing would help support prices in the long run.

data.title: Diwali 2026: Stock market enters Samvat 2083 with Nifty 50 above 25,000: Key support, resistance levels. Targets to know
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Indian equity markets are entering Samvat 2083 on a strong footing after an extraordinary week on Dalal Street, with the Nifty 50 reclaiming the psychologically important 25,000 mark and the Sensex crossing 81,000.

Both benchmark indices recorded their biggest weekly gains since February 2021, rising 8.6% and 8.8%, respectively, as a sharp correction in crude oil prices, aggressive foreign fund buying and better-than-expected corporate earnings triggered a broad-based improvement in investor sentiment.

The rally was particularly significant as Indian equities managed to outperform global markets despite a sharp selloff in technology stocks and AI-linked shares. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs), who had remained net sellers for much of 2026, returned aggressively to domestic equities. They purchased shares worth Rs.13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data, taking their purchases over the last five trading sessions to Rs.35,781 crore, according to market estimates.

On Friday, 6 November, the Nifty 50 advanced 493.75 points, or 2.01%, to close at 25,030.35, while the BSE Sensex surged 1,718.01 points, or 2.17%, to settle at 81,028.02. Both indices ended at their highest levels in more than eight months. The Nifty and Sensex also extended their winning streaks to seven consecutive sessions, their longest such runs in 14 months and 26 months, respectively.

Despite the sharp recovery, both benchmarks remain in negative territory for 2026, with the Nifty down 4.2% and the Sensex lower by 4.9%, compared with a 7% gain in the MSCI Emerging Markets index.

With the festive season ushering in Samvat 2083, investors will be watching whether the momentum can be sustained or the sharp rally gives way to some consolidation. What are the key support and resistance levels for the Nifty 50, and how high can the index climb? Here's what market experts and technical analysts expect.

Dr V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments Limited, said the sharp selloff in US technology stocks could have a relatively limited impact on Indian equities, while the slowdown in the global AI trade could work in India's favour.

He attributed the Nasdaq's 5.6% plunge to concerns over a potential slowdown in data centre spending amid political opposition to large-scale investments in the sector in the US. According to him, the resulting correction in technology and AI-linked stocks could benefit markets such as India, which have relatively limited exposure to the global AI trade.

Vijayakumar noted that FIIs had purchased Indian equities worth Rs.35,781 crore over the preceding five trading sessions. He expects domestic markets to remain resilient if foreign buying continues, even as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) book profits.

He also highlighted that the ongoing rally is fundamentally supported by better-than-expected corporate earnings growth.

"An important factor investors should recognise is that this rally is being driven by large-cap stocks, which had become attractively valued," Vijayakumar said.

He pointed to the divergence between large- and small-cap stocks, noting that while the Sensex rallied 2.6% in the previous session, the Nifty Smallcap 100 index gained only 0.67%. This indicates that institutional money is increasingly moving towards large-cap stocks.

Vijayakumar sees further upside potential in financial, technology and automobile stocks.

Osho Krishan, Chief Manager - Technical and Derivatives Research at Angel One, said the Nifty 50 has staged a sharp vertical rally, decisively moving above all its key exponential moving averages (EMAs) and the 200-day simple moving average (200-DSMA).

However, momentum indicators have entered overbought territory, suggesting that investors should exercise caution at current levels. Krishan said some profit booking cannot be ruled out, but any such correction should be viewed as a healthy consolidation that could help sustain the broader bullish trend.

On the downside, he identified the 24,770-24,500 zone as immediate support, while the bullish gap around 24,300 remains a crucial support level.

On the upside, 25,150 could act as an intermediate hurdle, followed by resistance near 25,400.

Looking ahead, Krishan advised traders to adopt a stock-specific approach, particularly during the festive season and the truncated trading week. With the market having rallied sharply and technical indicators showing overbought conditions, he recommended a conservative approach and disciplined risk management.

"With most of the easy gains already captured, selective participation and prudent position sizing will be key," he said.

Rajesh Bhosale, Technical Analyst at My Advisor Alpha, said the sharp market recovery was driven by a combination of favourable global developments, aggressive foreign institutional buying and the unwinding of accumulated short positions.

He attributed the rally to the Democrats' sweeping victory in the US midterm elections, securing control of both the House and the Senate, which raised hopes of an early resolution to the US-Iran conflict. This triggered a sharp decline in crude oil prices from their six-month highs, providing significant relief to an oil-importing economy such as India.

Bhosale also highlighted the return of foreign investors, who had been persistent sellers through October, noting that they purchased around Rs.15,000 crore worth of Indian equities on Thursday alone. The unwinding of short positions further amplified the rally.

He said market sentiment had undergone a sharp turnaround in just a few weeks. The Nifty 50, which was struggling near its multi-year swing low of 22,200-22,500, has now reclaimed 25,000 and moved decisively above its major moving averages.

The index has also confirmed a bullish double-bottom breakout, while its daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) has surged above 78 from below 40 in just a week, indicating strong upward momentum.

"Given the pattern breakout, the positive momentum is likely to continue. However, after such a sharp rally and with overbought conditions in place, traders should adopt a buy-on-dips approach," Bhosale said.

He identified 24,800 as immediate support, which also marks the breakout zone. On the upside, 25,400-25,500 is the key resistance band. A decisive move above this zone could open the way towards 26,000 and fresh all-time highs.

Bhosale added that the latest rally was largely driven by heavyweight stocks, while participation from the mid-cap segment remained relatively limited. Going ahead, he expects the Nifty to consolidate after its sharp gains, with individual stocks, particularly mid-caps, potentially leading the next leg of the rally.

data.title: AstraZeneca Pharma India Reports 30% Revenue Growth, Crosses Rs 7,291 Mn
data.description:
Strong performance across oncology, biopharmaceuticals and rare diseases, alongside regulatory approvals and state-level healthcare partnerships, drives growth

AstraZeneca Pharma India Limited reported a 30 per cent year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 7,291 million in the second quarter of FY2026-27, covering July to September 2026, driven by sustained performance across its oncology, biopharmaceuticals and rare disease portfolios. The company also reported a 30 per cent increase in revenue for the first half of FY2026-27, reaching Rs 14,119 million, compared with Rs 10,854 million in the corresponding period last year. The company attributed its performance to operational efficiency, portfolio expansion and increasing adoption of innovative therapies addressing unmet medical needs in India.

Oncology remained the largest contributor, generating Rs 5,085 million in Q2, compared with Rs 3,978 million in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from biopharmaceuticals, covering cardiovascular, renal and metabolism (CVRM), respiratory and immunology (R&I), and vaccines and immunotherapies (V&I), stood at Rs 1,610 million, against Rs 1,268 million previously. The rare diseases segment recorded revenue of Rs 204 million, compared with Rs 38 million in the corresponding quarter last year.

Regulatory Approvals And Expansion

Commenting on the results, Praveen Rao Akkinepally, Country President and Managing Director, AstraZeneca Pharma India, said the growth reflected the strength of the company's science-led portfolio and its ability to translate innovation into meaningful patient outcomes.

During the quarter, the company secured multiple regulatory approvals, including new indications for trastuzumab deruxtecan across HER2-positive breast cancer settings. Approvals were also received for benralizumab for hypereosinophilic syndrome and acalabrutinib-based combinations for previously untreated chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and mantle cell lymphoma.

The company also expanded its healthcare partnerships through memoranda of understanding with the governments of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. These collaborations aim to strengthen oncology care, genomic testing and AI-enabled lung cancer screening across public healthcare facilities.

Other initiatives included K+ Connect, focused on hyperkalaemia management among patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease, and India Coronary Conquest 2026, aimed at strengthening cardiovascular care through clinician-led learning. AstraZeneca Pharma India also received recognition at the OPPI India Awards 2026 for its rare disease contributions and at the ETHRWorld Employee Experience Awards 2026, where it secured a Gold Award.

data.title: Culture Evolves When People Act Without Reminders: Alembic CHRO On Lasting Change
data.description:
Namita Patwari says lasting change needs employee involvement, visible leadership commitment and open feedback, and that the real test of a cultural shift is what people do when no one is reminding them of the new behaviours

At 115 years old, Alembic Pharmaceuticals is evolving without letting go of what defines it. Namita Patwari, CHRO and Chief Customer Experience Officer, says HR’s job is to protect trust, integrity, commitment and purpose while building the digital fluency, analytical thinking and adaptability pharma will need. She explains how AI-enabled learning through RepReadyAI is strengthening field execution, why wellbeing must be built into how work is organised and not run as a stand-alone programme, and why a culture has truly shifted only when people act on new behaviours without being reminded. She also outlines what HR should do early to make mergers and partnerships work, beginning with listening.

A 115-year-old company keeps evolving without losing its identity. Which elements of a long-standing culture should HR deliberately protect as the business changes?

The strength of a legacy organisation lies in evolving while staying true to its values. At Alembic, over a century of growth has been guided by trust, integrity, commitment, and purpose. HR plays a key role in preserving this legacy while adapting to changing employee expectations and business needs. Culture is reflected in everyday actions, leadership decisions, and how employees feel respected, valued, and included. A strong legacy fosters belonging and pride while creating opportunities for growth, enabling employees to contribute meaningfully to the organisation’s future.

Which capabilities will pharma need most over the next five years, and how should HR build them across R&D, manufacturing, and commercial teams?

I believe the pharmaceutical industry will increasingly require digital fluency, analytical thinking, technical expertise, and adaptability. Equally important is the ability to learn continuously and apply knowledge effectively in everyday work. At Alembic, our RepReadyAI initiative reflects how technology can make learning more interactive, practical, and engaging.

For me, the real value of learning lies not in completing a programme, but in how confidently employees apply their knowledge, improve their performance, and grow in their roles. Learning outcomes should be measurable through stronger on-the-job application, improved productivity, enhanced quality of execution, and increased readiness for larger responsibilities.

HR must create opportunities for continuous learning through relevant development programmes, practical exposure, and regular feedback. We must also help employees prepare for evolving responsibilities and future career opportunities. Equally important is tracking the effectiveness of learning through indicators such as skill proficiency, performance improvements, internal mobility, succession readiness, and the successful application of new capabilities in the workplace. When people are equipped to grow alongside the business and learning outcomes are translated into tangible results, capability building becomes an investment in both individual development and organisational resilience.

As AI takes over more routine HR work, how will the role of the CHRO change in the next few years?

I see AI as an opportunity to make HR more proactive, efficient, and data-driven by simplifying routine processes and enabling greater focus on leadership development, workforce planning, capability building, and employee experience. In pharma, AI can help identify skill gaps across functions, anticipate future capability needs, personalise learning, and strengthen talent pipelines. At Alembic, RepReadyAI demonstrates how AI-enabled, practice-based learning can strengthen scientific knowledge, customer engagement, and field execution among sales representatives.

However, the human dimension of HR will remain critical. While AI can provide insights, understanding employee aspirations, building trust, coaching leaders, and making sensitive people decisions require empathy and judgement. CHROs must ensure technology complements human capabilities while helping employees develop digital fluency and adaptability.

Ultimately, AI’s value must be measured through tangible outcomes, including faster onboarding and hiring, improved learning effectiveness and field productivity, stronger GMP and compliance training adherence, better succession readiness, and enhanced employee engagement. Used thoughtfully, AI can enable better decisions and build a more agile, responsive, and future-ready organisation.

How can wellbeing become part of the way work is organised, rather than a stand-alone programme?

I believe wellbeing is shaped by everyday work experiences-how we respect people’s time, understand their needs, and support them through different stages of life. At Alembic, the eight-hour workday and period-related work-from-home flexibility reflect this focus. I believe such measures recognise employees’ diverse needs and responsibilities while enabling them to contribute effectively.

For me, a supportive culture also means creating an environment where employees can raise concerns comfortably and managers lead with empathy. For example, a manager adjusting a deadline when an employee faces a personal challenge demonstrates how small, thoughtful actions can make wellbeing part of everyday work. Policies provide the framework, but their impact lies in how they are practised. I believe wellbeing must be reflected in daily decisions, team interactions, and opportunities for growth and not treated as a stand-alone HR initiative.

With your grounding in organisation development, what makes a change initiative last, and what tells you a culture has genuinely shifted?

One of the most important lessons I have learnt is that change cannot be sustained through communication alone. People embrace change when they understand its purpose, see its relevance to their work, and witness leaders consistently demonstrating the expected behaviours. In my experience, lasting change requires employee involvement, visible leadership commitment, and opportunities to share feedback and concerns. When employees feel heard and included, they take ownership rather than view change as something imposed on them.

For me, a real cultural shift is reflected in everyday actions like how teams collaborate, take accountability, make decisions, and express different viewpoints. While engagement scores and employee feedback are useful indicators, I believe the true measure of success lies in what people do when no one is reminding them what the new behaviours should be. Change becomes sustainable when these behaviours become part of the organisation's way of working and are reflected naturally in how people think, interact and contribute every day. That, to me, is when culture has genuinely evolved.

As companies grow through partnerships and acquisitions, what should HR put in place early so that different cultures come together well?

I believe successful cultural integration begins with listening. Every organisation has its own strengths, values and working styles, and HR should understand these before deciding how to bring people together. A culture and working-style assessment of both organisations, done early, gives integration decisions a factual base. Early on, HR must give clarity on roles, reporting lines, communication channels and growth opportunities, and commit to timelines for each. Uncertainty is where people disengage or leave, so concerns should be addressed openly, with critical talent engaged first and regular forums such as town halls and Q&As where employees can ask questions and get honest answers.

I would place strong emphasis on leadership alignment. Leaders from both sides should present a consistent message and model the behaviours expected. A joint integration team, along with cross-team projects built around shared goals, helps relationships form through real work. Integration should not mean overlooking the strengths each group brings; the aim is to keep what works from both and build a common purpose people can connect with. Ultimately, integration succeeds when employees see a place for themselves in the organisation’s future and understand how they can contribute to it. That sense of belonging is what holds a combined organisation together.

Savi Khanna

data.title: Amber Enterprises Arm IL JIN Electronics Files DRHP For Rs 2,500 Cr IPO
data.description:
Amber Enterprises subsidiary plans a Rs 2,500 crore fresh issue to pare debt, fund manufacturing equipment purchases and support capacity expansion across its electronics manufacturing operations.

IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd, a subsidiary of Amber Enterprises India Ltd, has filed draft papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to raise Rs 2,500 crore through an initial public offering (IPO), according to its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6.

The proposed IPO will comprise entirely a fresh issue of equity shares, with no offer for sale (OFS) component, meaning the proceeds will go to the company.

IL JIN Electronics plans to use the IPO proceeds to repay or prepay outstanding borrowings, along with accrued interest, availed by the company and its subsidiaries, Ascent Circuits and Shogini Technoarts. The funds will also be deployed towards purchasing plant, machinery and equipment for its manufacturing facilities, besides meeting general corporate requirements.

The company operates as a vertically integrated electronics design and manufacturing services provider across four business segments: electronics manufacturing services (EMS), bare printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing, power electronics and industrial automation.

IL JIN Electronics currently operates 11 manufacturing facilities, including 10 in India and one in Israel. Its domestic manufacturing footprint spans Noida and Greater Noida in Uttar Pradesh, Pune in Maharashtra, Chennai and Hosur in Tamil Nadu, and Bengaluru in Karnataka.

The company also has six manufacturing facilities under construction, which are expected to add to its production capacity as it expands operations.

Financially, IL JIN Electronics reported revenue from operations of Rs 3,268.47 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 1,240.41 crore in FY24.

Its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased to Rs 321.07 crore in FY26 from Rs 71.42 crore in FY24, reflecting an expansion in both its business scale and operating earnings over the two-year period.

Amber Enterprises is a major player in India's room air-conditioner original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and original design manufacturer (ODM) market. The proposed listing of IL JIN Electronics will provide the group with a separate listed platform for its electronics manufacturing operations.

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Axis Capital and Jefferies India have been appointed as the book-running lead managers for the IPO, while KFin Technologies will serve as the registrar to the issue.
